import createContext.description: Type-safe context for loaders, actions and middleware. Not React's `createContext`.

createContext().description:
Creates a typed key for passing values through the request lifecycle.
Read and written with `context.get(key)` / `context.set(key, value)` — a default value makes reads safe before it is set.

context.get() in loader.description: Read a value a middleware placed into the request context.

context.set() in middleware.description: Store a value for the loaders and actions further down the chain.

import RouterContextProvider.description: Container for context values, returned from a custom server's `getLoadContext`.

RouterContextProvider().description:
Build the load context in a custom server.
With the middleware flag on, `getLoadContext` must return this instead of a plain object.

createCookie().description: **Framework mode.** A signed, typed cookie. Parse with `await cookie.parse(request.headers.get('Cookie'))`, write with `await cookie.serialize(value)`.

cookie parse / serialize.description: **Framework mode.** Read a cookie in a loader and write it back on the response.

import createCookieSessionStorage.description: **Framework mode.** Session storage backed by a cookie.

body: export const { getSession, commitSession, destroySession } = createCookieSessionStorage({
createCookieSessionStorage().description:
**Framework mode.** The usual session setup: the whole session lives in a signed cookie, so no server store is needed.
Size is capped at ~4kb — keep only ids in it.

session read / commit.description:
**Framework mode.** Read a session in a loader/action and persist any changes with `commitSession`.
Every mutation needs the `Set-Cookie` header, or the change is lost.

session flash message.description:
**Framework mode.** A value read exactly once, then removed — the standard post-redirect toast.
Read it with `session.get('message')` in the next loader.

body: export const { getSession, commitSession, destroySession } = createMemorySessionStorage({
createMemorySessionStorage().description: **Framework mode.** Keeps sessions in memory. For tests and local development only — everything is lost on restart, and it does not survive multiple processes.

body: export const { getSession, commitSession, destroySession } = createSessionStorage({
createSessionStorage().description:
**Framework mode.** Custom-backed sessions — the cookie holds only an id, the data lives in your store (DB, Redis, KV).
Use this when sessions exceed the cookie size limit or must be revocable server-side.

isCookie() / isSession().description: **Framework mode.** Type guards for the cookie and session objects. Mostly useful inside libraries and adapters.
